attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his 2025 predictions post, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: Faithful. The testable core is the trend in prevalence. 'Less than I feared' compares outcomes with his own fears, and the call for vigilance is normative.

contract.note: Reading 'widespread' as distribution and requiring a documented prior expectation for the fear comparison is a fair, ordinary reading. The result depends on that interpretation.

evidence.note: NewsGuard's own monitoring: identified AI news sites grew from 49 to 600+ in 2023 under fixed criteria. This supports wider distribution, with the caveat that counts depend on discovery.
Secondary report of NewsGuard's count of 966 sites by July 2024, which suggests continued growth. It does not measure audience or effects.
Pre-election reporting that AI's effects were limited. There is no baseline for Marcus's fears, and it covers only part of the period.

reviews.rationale: The part saying AI misinformation became more widespread is supported by NewsGuard's site counts for 2023–24. The contract also needs a documented prior expectation to show effects were smaller than Marcus feared, and the packet has none. TIME suggests limited effects, but it is partial context. Overall, the evidence does not settle the full claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words about OpenAI in his review of 2024.

semantics.note: Faithful. It has four parts: no profits, a company expectation of no profit before 2029, billions in burn, and no clear technical moat.

contract.note: Reading the claim as calendar 2024 with net cash burn is reasonable. The contract does not let a reported loss stand in for cash burn, which is strict but defensible. 'Moat' has no test, so the interpretation determines the result.

evidence.note: CNBC confirmed that OpenAI expected about $5B in 2024 losses. This is an estimate, not realized accounts or cash burn, though it is consistent with no profits.
Contemporary secondary reporting, based on The Information, that OpenAI did not expect yearly profits for five years. This supports the 2029-expectation part.
OpenAI's own disclosure that o1 was a technical advance. It does not establish a durable moat either way.

reviews.rationale: Reporting supports the 2029 profit expectation, and the expected $5B loss for 2024 is consistent with no profits. However, the packet has no matching record of net cash burn, and nothing settles whether OpenAI had a durable technical moat. The packet supports some parts and refutes none, but the contract's full support condition is not met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction, listed under 'High confidence' among his predictions for the end of 2025.

semantics.note: Firm 'will', filed under high confidence, so it is scored. 'Perhaps years' is correctly treated as optional. The horizon is the end of 2025.

contract.note: Reading it as a continuing pattern across several products, and treating Pro-only access at $200 a month as restricted, is a fair, ordinary reading. Affordability is the evaluator's judgment.

evidence.note: Operator was previewed on Jan 23, 2025 for US Pro users only, and was folded into ChatGPT agent about six months later.
ChatGPT agent's July rollout to Plus users still described the product as early stage, with mistakes and regional limits.
Pulse was previewed in September 2025 for Pro mobile users only, with Plus to follow later.
Release notes from Dec 17, 2025 confirm Pulse was still Pro-only, nearly three months after its preview.
OpenAI's own page gives the $200-a-month price of Pro, which is context for affordability.
Deep research reached Plus users within weeks. This is a counterexample to a fixed pattern but does not refute the continuing practice.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2025) has passed. At least two 2025 previews, Operator and Pulse, stayed restricted to the premium tier for months: about six months, and nearly three months as of mid-December. The quicker Plus rollout of deep research is an exception, not a refutation. The multi-month pattern the forecast described held.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his review of 2024.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps the comparison with 'most people expected', the all-companies scope, and the hardware exclusion.

contract.note: The plain reading (generative AI, 2024, excluding hardware) is fair. The company universe, expectation baseline and accounting basis are not stated, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Census data show low but rising business AI use through August 2024, using a broad definition of AI. There is no matched measure of earlier expectations.
A forecast of about $5B in losses for one company, OpenAI. It is not a realized total for the industry.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no matched evidence comparing 2024 adoption with earlier expectations, and no industry-wide profit total on a known accounting basis. Low Census adoption rates and OpenAI's projected loss are consistent with the claim but do not establish either part.
